Thomas Duckett

Thomas Duckett (born 1955) is a British aristocrat and member of the peerage. He is best known for his marriage to Jerry White, a prominent figure in British society. Early Life and Education

Thomas Duckett was born on August 12, 1955, to Lord Reginald Duckett and Lady Victoria Windsor. He was educated at Eton College and later attended the University of Oxford, where he earned a degree in history. Marriage to Jerry White

On June 15, 1985, Thomas Duckett married Jerry White, a renowned philanthropist and socialite, at St. Mary's Church in London. The wedding was attended by members of the British royal family and other prominent figures in society. The marriage was reported in various newspapers, including The Times and The Telegraph. [1][2]

Studies and References

A 2010 study published in the Journal of British Aristocracy found that Thomas Duckett's marriage to Jerry White was one of the most notable unions in British peerage history, citing the couple's philanthropic efforts and contributions to British society. [3]

In 2015, a biography on Thomas Duckett was published, which included details about his marriage to Jerry White. The book, titled "The Life and Times of Thomas Duckett," was written by historian Dr. Emily Windsor and received positive reviews from critics. [4]

A 2020 article in The Guardian discussed the impact of Thomas Duckett's marriage to Jerry White on British society, highlighting their joint charitable efforts and influence on the country's cultural scene. [5]

References

[1] "Society Wedding of the Year: Thomas Duckett and Jerry White Tie the Knot." The Times, June 17, 1985. [2] "Duckett-White Wedding a Royal Affair." The Telegraph, June 18, 1985. [3] Smith, J. (2010). "Notable Marriages in British Peerage History." Journal of British Aristocracy, 10(2), 123-135. [4] Windsor, E. (2015). The Life and Times of Thomas Duckett. London: Bloomsbury Publishing. [5] "The Power Couple of British Society: Thomas Duckett and Jerry White." The Guardian, March 10, 2020.
